title: Qwen3.5-4B Q4_K_M — llama.cpp on 8 GB Macs and 8 GB laptop GPUs
slug_note: The card's own llama-server command at 2.71 GB: fits the 5.3 GB Metal budget of an 8 GB Mac and 7.5 GB of VRAM on an RTX 4060.

variation.quant_detail: qwen35-4b-Q4_K_M.gguf (2.71 GB, HF tree), self-quantized from Qwen's original weights with a per-tensor imatrix

engine.config: llama.cpp llama-server; -hf pulls the Q4_K_M quant directly, --jinja applies the Qwen3.5 chat template, -c 8192 context. Metal on Apple Silicon, CUDA on NVIDIA.

requirements.notes: Estimate: 2.71 GB Q4_K_M file + 8192-token KV ≈ 3.5 GB — fits the 5.3 GB default Metal budget of an 8 GB Mac and the 7.5 GB usable VRAM of an 8 GB laptop GPU. The 8 GB tier's own notes state a 4-bit 4B fits and a 9B does not.

steps.text: Install llama.cpp (brew install llama.cpp on macOS, winget install llama.cpp on Windows; see Step 0 in Quick start).
Open the local Web UI or point a client at the served OpenAI-compatible endpoint.

caveats: No laptop measurement recorded: status untested. The exact command ran as written on our DGX Spark on 2026-11-16; that box's speeds do not carry over to 8 GB laptops.
On an 8 GB Mac the browser and the model share the same pool — close other apps first (see the mac-8gb tier notes).
The repo ships text-only quants — it carries no vision projector, so this lane has no image input even though the base model is multimodal.
The card insists on --jinja: without the chat template the model can emit malformed turns.

sources.note: card's Get started section states the llama-server command verbatim; quant sizes from the repo tree
